letter.subject: Concern about cookie and tracking practices on halma.com following rejection of cookies
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified during an automated, passive privacy audit of https://halma.com on 2026-11-08 04:11 UTC. Using a fresh browser, we clicked the cookie banner’s reject option (“Decline cookies”) and recorded what was still sent while browsing https://www.halma.com/who-we-are, https://www.halma.com/our-companies and https://www.halma.com/how-we-grow. We also reviewed your privacy policy at https://www.halma.com/site-services/data-privacy.

Our findings are as follows:

1. After cookies were rejected, Google still received data. We observed 13 requests to doubleclick.net and youtube.com after rejection. We also observed new tracking cookies being set after rejection: VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, VISITOR_PRIVACY_METADATA, YSC and __Secure-YNID. Our review suggests this may involve non-essential advertising-related tracking continuing without consent.

2. We observed one tracking company that does not appear to be named in the privacy policy. The policy names 5 companies. We saw Google, but found no mention of Google by name. We recognise the policy may describe recipients only by category, for example “advertising partners”, but our review suggests this may not clearly identify the recipient.

3. We observed device fingerprinting activity from google.com after cookies were rejected. Scripts from google.com (https://www.google.com/js/th/n_BHgtbTP3l_ff810bu_K6lL5wb_ZK3aoRJMIVk8Tks.js) used WebGL (GPU model) fingerprinting after rejection. Our review suggests this appears to involve accessing information from a user’s device without consent.

Please would you:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential tracking that occurs without consent.
4. Reply within one month of this letter.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker

ai_review.summary: The audit evidence indicates serious post-rejection advertising, tracking-cookie and fingerprinting activity, but those issues are already covered by the automated checks and are not repeated here. The policies identify Halma plc and explain several processing purposes and user rights, but the privacy policy does not clearly name Google as a recipient or provide a complete retention framework for personal data.
evidence: E1: Cookie banner found: True. Reject clicked successfully: True. Method: selector. Buttons clicked: Decline cookies.
E2: Fingerprinting by scripts from google.com: webgl; phases: after_reject.

E3: Tracker Google (Advertising): 0 requests before consent, 13 after reject, to doubleclick.net, youtube.com. Example after-reject requests: https://www.youtube.com/embed/Lpl3chRg1Qw?si=um7dp8IrX8HvVkpP&enablejsapi=1&origin=https://halma-corp-v2.cm.invdcloud-is.co.uk | https://www.youtube.com/s/player/a5c2aafe/www-player.css
E4: Tracking cookie YSC from Google on .youtube.com present after reject (NEW, not present before); session cookie.
E5: Tracking cookie VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE from Google on .youtube.com present after reject (NEW, not present before); expires in 180 days; holds what looks like a unique ID.
E6: Tracking cookie VISITOR_PRIVACY_METADATA from Google on .youtube.com present after reject (NEW, not present before); expires in 180 days.
E7: Tracking cookie __Secure-YNID from Google on .youtube.com present after reject (NEW, not present before); expires in 180 days; holds what looks like a unique ID.
E8: Empty cookie __Secure-ROLLOUT_TOKEN (Google) present after reject: it holds no value, so it stores nothing about the user.
E9: Pages browsed and scrolled after reject: https://www.halma.com/who-we-are, https://www.halma.com/our-companies, https://www.halma.com/how-we-grow.
E10: Privacy policy: https://www.halma.com/site-services/data-privacy. Companies it names: Investis Digital, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter. Contact email found: dataprotection@halma.com.

E12: Automated check (high): Google still received data after you rejected cookies. 13 requests to doubleclick.net, youtube.com after you clicked reject (Advertising). New tracking cookies set after reject: VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, VISITOR_PRIVACY_METADATA, YSC, __Secure-YNID.

E13: Automated check (medium): 1 tracking company not named in the privacy policy. The policy names 5 companies. We saw these and found no mention: Google. (The policy may describe them only by category, e.g. 'advertising partners'.)

E14: Automated check (medium): google.com fingerprinted your device (WebGL (GPU model)). Scripts from google.com (https://www.google.com/js/th/n_BHgtbTP3l_ff810bu_K6lL5wb_ZK3aoRJMIVk8Tks.js) used WebGL (GPU model) fingerprinting after you rejected cookies.
